title: First-mover safety runbook & pilot cohort notes
content:
Purpose
This is a personal runbook & scratchpad for running a very conservative first-mover / pilot cohort during model flips or infra changes (kernel swap, quantization profile updates, batching change). Goal is to capture heuristics, safety checkpoints, and quick recovery recipes that I can reuse and hand to on-call. Not a policy doc — operational notes + live checklist + hypotheses.

Context and scope
- When: low-risk pilot windows (off-peak region/weekend before broad flip).
- Who: small external cohort (5–10 tenants) + internal shadow traffic.
- What: validate latency SLOs, token-cost delta, and small-scale quality checks on 10 canonical prompts.
- Assumptions: new runtime change is backward-compatible; model flavor has a near-identical tokenizer; KV cache warmup behaves similar.

Quick TL;DR checklist (one-liners)
- ✅ Preflight: snapshot current routing config + pinned versions (api-routes, model pins).
- ✅ Sanity: run smoke script against canary infra (smoke-canary.sh) to confirm endpoints respond in < 200ms p50.
- ✅ Client pin: allocate pilot cohort in routing with 0.5% traffic or explicit tenant list.
- ✅ Telemetry: create temporary dashboard (pilot-<date>) with latency/cost/err rates and add to on-call rotation.
- ✅ Eval: push canonical prompt set (pilot-10) through new variant and baseline for diff scoring.
- ⛔ Escape: hot-pin back to baseline if error-rate > 0.5% absolute or median latency regresses > 30% or median quality delta > 0.08 (metric TBD).

Detailed preflight (run before any traffic)
- Config snapshot: curl admin://config/snapshot -> store as artifacts/configs/pilot-<date>.json (create linked artifact in ticket).
- Traffic plan: create routing rule: route.pilot = {tenants: [t-123, t-234], fraction: 0.005, sticky: true}. Double-check sticky cookie TTL matches tenant affinity model.
- Pinning: ensure model artifact id is pinned in tenant override for pilot list and that rollout flags are explicit.
- Observability: create short-lived dashboard with these panels: p50/p95 latency, cpu/gpu utilization, token-per-request distribution, model inference errors, client retry spikes, quant dropout (if exposed). Add tag pilot-<date>.
- Canary probes: warm-up 30k tokens across family of prompts to populate KV cache. Expect latency tail to drop substantially after warmup.

Runtime probes & heuristics
- Warmup sequencing: start with low concurrency single-tenant warmups; then add parallel warmup across tenants to simulate KV pressure. If p95 increases > 2x during warmup, abort and investigate cache eviction cadence.
- Memory knob: if OOMs appear, reduce batch size and enable strict kv-eviction: true. Note: enabling eviction may increase cold-start latency for some cohorts.
- Kernel swap note: after kernel swap, verify same batch-size throughput using synthetic perf harness. If throughput delta > 15% backoff to canary with reduced batch size.

Quality verification (manual + automated)
- Run pilot-10 prompt set on both baseline and new variant. Capture: BLEU-like loose score (token overlap), hallucination count (manual quick pass), and semantic drift (embedding-based similarity).
- Manual triage: sample 10 real user queries across the pilot tenants and run side-by-side in a private thread. Tag anything with obvious truncation/formatting regressions.

Failure modes and immediate mitigations
- Elevated HTTP 5xx from model service: switch routing to baseline variant, mark canary instance unhealthy, collect logs (model stderr, runtime trace).
- Latency tail spike with normal p50: throttle incoming concurrency for pilot cohort, reduce batch size and enable isolation mode for pilot GPUs.
- Quality regressions: immediate pin back for affected tenants and open a quick incident note in ticket (JIRA-2458).

Rollforward criteria (what must be true to expand traffic)
- 72-hour window with no regression in p95 beyond 20% of baseline and no quality alerts from customer success.
- Cost delta per token < 12% unless justified by quality improvements.
- No more than one emergent bug (non-trivial fix) in the 72-hour period.

Rollout plan (staged)
1) Internal smoke (internal tenants + shadow): < 2 hours.
2) Pilot tenants (explicit list): 0.5% traffic, 24–48h observation.
3) Soft ramp: 2% traffic for 24h if metrics steady.
4) Regional expansion: add next region at 1% then ramp.
5) Full flip: coordinate with release-engineering and marketing if public-facing.

Notes to self / gotchas
- Don’t trust p50 during warmup. p95 and error-rate are king.
- Watch for correlated client retries — they can amplify perceived latency issues. Add a client-side jitter recommendation to pilot tenants temporarily.
- If using quantized model variant, run a cheap eval to catch formatting regressions (numbers, dates) — quantization sometimes scrambles decimal formatting in edge cases.

Open questions & TODOs
- Define exact quality delta threshold (currently using placeholder 0.08). Need to sync with applied-ml on metric definition (embedding sim vs human score). ACTION: book 30m with Lina (applied-ml).
- Should we have an automated abort if CPU socket temperature crosses threshold? Who owns infra alert? ACTION: ping SRE rotation.
- Add checklist item: inform sales for any pilot tenant that is revenue > $50k ARR.

Immediate next steps (for today)
- Finish dashboard panels + share with Evan and Maya (already in collaborators).
- Run smoke-canary.sh against staging canary and paste output to JIRA-2458.
- Draft brief for pilot tenants that explains expected behavior and escape hatch.

Appendix: useful commands
- Snapshot config: curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/config/snapshot -d '{"tag":"pilot-2025-01-10"}'
- Smoke script: ./scripts/smoke-canary.sh --variant=pilot --prompts=pilot-10 --concurrency=4
- Quick pin back: curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/routing/pin -d '{"tenants":["t-123"], "to":"baseline"}'

(End of scratchpad — this is intentionally informal, will iterate to a cleaned runbook if we repeat this flow.)
